candidates.name: Web Coverage Service Standard
verified_facts: WCS provides electronic retrieval of geospatial coverages.
WCS 2.0.1 is an OGC core interface standard.
Coverage service behavior is extended by separate CRS, interpolation, scaling and encoding extensions.
semantic_limits: WCS conformance describes service behavior and does not itself prove a particular returned elevation value is correct.

candidates.name: WCS Interpolation Extension 1.0
verified_facts: The extension lets a GetCoverage request control interpolation during server-side coverage processing.
Interpolation affects operations including scaling and CRS change.
semantic_limits: Interpolation choice must be explicit when server-side resampling occurs; it must not be assumed from output appearance.

candidates.name: WCS Earth Observation Application Profile
verified_facts: The profile requires support for the WCS CRS Extension.
It requires at least one supported coverage encoding such as GeoTIFF, NetCDF or JPEG2000.
semantic_limits: Supported encodings and CRS capabilities are transport/service properties, not parcel-level accuracy guarantees.

candidates.name: Persistent LIDAR WCS services announcement
verified_facts: EA publishes persistent WCS endpoints for LIDAR Composite DTM 1m and 2m.
The published GetCapabilities examples use WCS version 2.0.1.
The persistent endpoint naming is intended to remain stable across future updates.
semantic_limits: Endpoint persistence does not guarantee every request or subset is valid; coverage identifiers and request parameters still require readback validation.

candidates.name: National Grid Transformation OSTN15
verified_facts: OSTN15 is the definitive OSGB36/ETRS89 transformation.
It uses 1 km transformation grids and bilinear interpolation.
A simple Helmert transformation is only suitable for roughly 3 m accuracy applications.
semantic_limits: OSTN15 is a horizontal datum transformation and is distinct from vertical ODN/OSGM15 handling.

candidates.name: Coordinate reference systems
verified_facts: British National Grid uses OSGB36 and Transverse Mercator eastings/northings in metres.
BNG is a horizontal spatial reference system only and does not specify a vertical height reference system.
semantic_limits: EPSG:27700 alone is insufficient to describe ODN heights; vertical datum evidence must remain explicit.

candidates.name: OS NGD coordinate reference systems
verified_facts: OS NGD lists British National Grid as EPSG:27700.
It separately lists British National Grid plus ODN Height as EPSG:7405.
semantic_limits: Compound CRS identification does not change the canonical raster values; it is used to prevent horizontal/vertical reference conflation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 source data
verified_facts: Terrain 5 represents the bare-earth surface with X/Y eastings/northings and Z heights.
Buildings, supported structures and vegetation are excluded from the DTM.
Most mainland heights are relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
semantic_limits: Terrain 5 remains secondary sanity evidence because its resolution and accuracy are insufficient for the primary sub-metre parcel result.

candidates.name: Transverse Mercator map projections
verified_facts: Map projection from the ellipsoid to a plane necessarily introduces distance and/or angular distortion.
British National Grid uses a Transverse Mercator projection with a central meridian at 2 degrees west and scale factor about 0.9996.
semantic_limits: Projection-scale effects are distinct from vertical elevation error and must not be merged into the LiDAR RMSE budget.

candidates.name: Future of British mapping coordinate systems
verified_facts: OSGB36 and ODN are retained as the basis of OS mapping.
OSTN15 and OSGM15 provide transformations from ETRS89/GNSS to national horizontal and vertical datums.
semantic_limits: Datum continuity is reference-system evidence and does not independently validate parcel sampling or source freshness.
